    Read the numbers
    Challenge the assumptionsCoordination, handoffs & model limits+

    Six specialists, one capability each. Moving a card changes team membership, not headcount. Bigger teams lose more time to internal coordination; crossing a boundary adds delay and receiving effort.

    Illustrative defaults: 5% per teammate, 0.75 days per crossing. Receiving a handoff also takes 0.15 effort points.

    The mechanism

    Capability capacity = 1 − coordination loss × (team size − 1)

    Every piece of work follows a fixed sequence. Each capability serves its oldest ready work first. Specialist capacity cannot be borrowed by another capability. A wider team may save transfers while slowing its busiest specialist.

    The model advances in quarter-day steps. All capabilities work simultaneously before completed stages move on. Only team boundaries change between compared layouts; their workload and assumptions are identical.

    A thinking model, not staffing advice

    Work, coefficients and examples are fictional. No learning, parallel stages, skill overlap, rework, priorities or managerial hierarchy. There is no cost to reorganising: a move replays an alternative history.
